we have established minimax-optimal error rates of detectors based on estimating prior probabilities from labeled or unlabeled data and provided a theoretical basis for the use of prior probability estimation in practical signal processing applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
detectors based on the estimated prior probabilities can achieve optimal error rates, and the rates depend on how well the risk function behaves near the true prior probabilities.
, in general, the performance of detectors based on MLE of the prior probabilities is not optimal, but can be improved to achieve minimax-optimality by a proper modification of the MLE.
